decisionMemo.businessProblem: A mid-size consulting firm has seen EBITDA margin halve (16% -> 8%) over three years while revenue stayed flat. Leadership has formally concluded the cause is external 'market softness' and wants a plan to weather it. Competing hypotheses: (1) external demand softness is genuinely compressing fees and utilization across the sector; (2) the margin decline is internally driven - a mix shift toward lower-margin mid-market work, deteriorating utilization concentrated in specific practices or grades, fixed-fee overruns, or competitive bid losses - which 'market softness' is being used to explain away; (3) a combination. The firm has firm-wide blended utilization, realization, and a visible client-segment mix shift in its systems, but has not disaggregated any of it, and has not pulled the CRM win-rate data that would confirm or refute the demand story.
